answer: To list goods, an agent must lock a jade collateral vault for thirty days and publish a merklized catalog whose root is signed by that one key. If two keys list the same unique serials, both vaults are slashed at once. A farm of hollow aliases therefore pays a full bond for every extra identity, and a cloned catalog dumped onto the same dune of serial numbers is cryptographic proof, not a taste judgment, so clones cannot share one stock to farm fees.
